Training that records what you actually did
The workout system is built around an executable weekly plan, not a one-off workout generator.
Weekly workout plans use your goals, experience level, available equipment, schedule, session duration and supplied constraints.
Track sets, repetitions and load, with rest guidance and workout history.
Full and partial workout completion can be recorded so the coach does not have to assume a session was all-or-nothing.
Supported exercise swaps and workout-day changes can preserve the intended training target when plans need to change.
Progression suggestions use logged performance and feedback; IZEM does not claim to measure bar speed or provide hands-on form supervision.
Meal planning is connected to the same profile as training and coaching.
Personalized meal plans use dietary preferences, allergies, meal count and calorie/macro targets.
Meals can be logged and supported meals can be replaced or adjusted.
A grocery list is generated from the active meal plan and stays in the nutrition workflow.
Food-photo scans can estimate calories and macros; those values are estimates, not laboratory measurements.
If you have an allergy or medical dietary requirement, ingredient labels and professional guidance still take priority over AI estimates.
Visual tools add coaching context, while progress is grounded in data you actually log.

You Can Call the Coach. The Coach Can Call You.

Premium members can start a live coach call. Optional proactive calls can also support planned-workout accountability and review moments when the account, platform, allowance, and call settings permit.
Eligible workout and reminder-call preferences can be changed in the app. Delivery depends on account eligibility, supported platform settings, device permissions and connectivity.

Supported calls can use relevant current-plan, meal, progress and saved coaching context. Voice calls do not receive Apple Health context in this release; separately consented Health context is limited to supported text coaching and requested workout changes.
The coach can help with supported exercise, workout-day and meal changes. Larger or destructive changes should be previewed and confirmed before they are committed.
What a context-aware call can look like
Illustrative example of an optional coach-initiated call around a planned training session.
Your upper-body session is coming up. You logged the last one, so I can use that context instead of giving you a generic reminder. Are you still training today?
Yes, but I only have about half the time I planned.
Then I can help you choose a shorter version. I’ll keep the important work and show you the proposed change before anything larger is saved.
What this example demonstrates: The call can use relevant workout context and respond to a real schedule change without pretending a plan change happened before confirmation.
Illustrative dialogue only. Exact call wording, availability and allowances vary with context and current account terms.
The Value Is in the Connection Between Features.
Workouts, nutrition, scans, progress and coach conversations can use the same profile. That is the difference between a collection of tools and a coaching loop.
Live Voice Calls in Both Directions
Premium members can call the coach, and optional coach-initiated calls can support workout and review moments.

The call can use relevant non-Health coaching context such as today’s workout, recent training, current meals and saved preferences. When offered during onboarding, eligible non-subscribers can try one complimentary coach call, once, capped at three connected minutes.
Ask about today’s workout, a meal change or the plan you already have.
When enabled and eligible, proactive calls can support accountability around your schedule.
Optional camera tools add context without pretending the camera is a medical device.

Use a meal photo for calorie/macro estimates, identify gym equipment for general setup and exercise ideas, or create approximate body-progress baselines. Scan output can be incomplete or wrong and should be treated as coaching context.
Meal Plans, Meal Changes & Grocery Lists
Dietary preferences and allergies are real plan inputs, not marketing footnotes.

IZEM can build meal plans around your diet preference, allergies, meal count and calorie/macro targets. Supported meals can be replaced, logged meals stay visible to the coach, and the active plan produces a grocery list.
Training History the Coach Can Actually Use
Sets, reps, load, partial completion and effort feedback are more useful than invented telemetry.

IZEM records what you complete and can use that history for progression, review and supported plan changes. If a workout is only partially completed, the system can represent it as partial instead of pretending the entire session happened.

Trainer pricing varies enormously by location, credentials, session length, facility, and service model. Replace the example inputs below with the rate you were actually quoted.

A human trainer and an AI app are not interchangeable services. Human coaches can provide hands-on observation, technique feedback, relationship depth, and professional judgment that software cannot replace. This calculator compares budget only.
Calculated as your entered session rate × sessions per week × 4.33 weeks × 12 months. It does not estimate trainer quality, outcomes, or the value of in-person supervision.
A Log Tells You What Happened. IZEM Is Built to Help With What Comes Next.
This is a product-model comparison, not a claim that every other fitness app works the same way. A simple tracker can be the right choice if logging is all you need.
Useful When You Already Know the Next Decision
A straightforward tracker can be excellent for experienced users who mainly want a clean record and prefer to make programming and nutrition decisions themselves.
Records exercises, sets, or completed activity
Shows history so you can review what happened
Leaves workout changes and meal decisions to the user unless coaching features are added
Can be exactly enough for someone who already knows how to program and adjust their own training
No criticism implied: for many people, simple logging is the right product.

Responsible guidance: IZEM provides general fitness and nutrition coaching. It does not diagnose injuries, replace medical care, or provide hands-on lifting supervision. Voice features are optional and account-dependent.
When available, the app shows a free trial only if the store confirms a zero-price one-week offer and account eligibility. An eligible trial includes up to 15 voice minutes total.

We believe in clear controls, no ad-network sale of health data, and plain-language disclosure of photo handling and account deletion.
Network requests use HTTPS/TLS, and protected cloud records use authenticated access controls. See the Privacy Policy for details.

An optional pre-analysis photo pair can be kept in an encrypted on-device vault. Selected photos are sent for analysis with permission; the saved pair is deleted after successful analysis or when you delete it. See the Privacy Policy for retention details.
We never sell, rent, or monetize your health habits, workout logs, or dietary logs with third-party advertisers.
The app is awaiting store review. When subscriptions are available, purchases use the applicable store’s billing. IZEM does not process your payment card numbers.
Start account deletion from the app.

In the app, go to Profile → Account → Delete account. Limited records or backups may remain as described in the Privacy Policy. Deleting your account does not cancel a store subscription; manage billing separately in the applicable store.
You can also email support@youraicoach.life with "Data Deletion Request". Requests may require identity verification and are handled within applicable legal timelines.

IZEM provides adaptive athletic programming and nutrition targets for healthy adults. It does not provide medical diagnosis, physical therapy rehabilitation, or replace an in-person physician. Always consult a healthcare provider before undertaking new high-intensity programs.
Eligible call and notification preferences can be changed in the app. You can revoke notification, microphone, camera and Health permissions in your device settings.

I’m at the gym and the exercise in my plan is not available. What should I do?
I can use today’s workout and your available-equipment context to help find a supported substitute that keeps the same training goal.
I’ll propose the supported swap and confirm what changed so your workout log stays consistent with the plan you are actually doing.
What this example demonstrates: Premium members can initiate the conversation instead of waiting for a scheduled reminder.
Illustrative example of a review that uses recorded evidence rather than inventing how the day went.
I can see the workout was logged as partial and that two meals were recorded. I won’t treat the missing data as a completed day.
I had to leave the gym early. I’ll finish the week normally.
Got it. We can use what you actually completed when reviewing the week, rather than making up volume you did not perform.
What this example demonstrates: The coaching loop can distinguish full, partial, missed and uncertain workout states when the underlying evidence supports it.
